title: Normalization of a valuation ring and its prolongations
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be a finite algebraic extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension], and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Let $C=\{x\in L:x\text{ satisfies a monic polynomial over }V\}$ be the integral closure of $V$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $C$ is a nonzero integral domain integral over $V$, with fraction field $L$. Its set of maximal ideals is nonempty. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$, the subring $C_{\mathfrak n}\subseteq L$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a valuation ring and $C_{\mathfrak n}\cap K=V$. Conversely, every valuation ring $W\subseteq L$ with fraction field $L$ and $W\cap K=V$ is $C_{\mathfrak n}$ for a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$. No henselian, Noetherian, separability, rank, or module-finiteness assumption on $C/V$ is made.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: valued-field background for the reference to Bourbaki, A.C., VI, §8. Normalization/prolongation input before Krasner; full normalization theorem is background, not asserted explicitly in ILO. Bourbaki, Commutative Algebra VI §8, extensions of valuations, WANTED. Local Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00I8 (section-valuation-rings), especially Tag 00IA (lemma-dominate) and Tag 00IC (lemma-valuation-ring-normal), supplies background but not this full assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-normalization-localizations] to the given inclusion $K\subseteq L$ and valuation ring $V$. Its normalization is literally our $C$, since both consist of the elements of $L$ satisfying monic polynomials over $V$. Its first two assertions give that $C$ is a nonzero integral domain integral over $V$, has fraction field $L$, and has a maximal ideal. Its localization assertion gives, for every maximal $\mathfrak n$, that $C_{\mathfrak n}$ is a valuation ring with $C_{\mathfrak n}\cap K=V$. Its converse applies to every valuation ring of $L$ restricting to $V$ and gives the required unique maximal ideal. Here a valuation ring of $L$ has fraction field $L$, made explicit in our statement. The cited theorem assumes exactly the same finite algebraic extension and valuation-ring hypotheses, with none of the extra assumptions excluded in the final sentence. This is reuse of a pre-existing independently split theorem, not a new lemma restating the item.
